evidence: bare_number_card: In seg1:start/mid/end the visual is one big number (15.9, then 79.5, then 126) inside a ring with a fixed '1998' label. It is a counter, not a demonstration, and it counts UP while the narration says the record dropped.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: At seg2:start/mid/end two identical yellow circles both read '8.3' and both are labelled 'Before 2016 (1988-2013)'. The narration's 'almost 30 seconds a year' since 2016 never appears, and the kicker says 'BEFORE 2016 (1988-2013) TOPS THE LIST', which is backwards.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The comparison machine bound the same row to both slots, so the post-2016 series (about 30 s/yr) was dropped. It also picked a rank/bubble machine for a before/after rate claim.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Show two rates side by side: about 8 s/yr before 2016 vs about 30 s/yr since 2016, labelled correctly. Draw them as the subject's own motion, e.g. two runners or stopwatches where the post-2016 one sheds seconds about 3.6x faster. Data should drive the faster one (pushing the stopwatch hand or lacing the carbon shoe), and the 30 should visibly outrun the 8.
